kind: diagnostic with true-map X-points; nothing here is deployable, selectable or an admission; no 238, no 357
question: how much score does a given reduction of X-point target error buy through the deployed finisher - asked by the second agent after D40's head pre-gate (10 percent on both ends) rejected all three families at 8-10 percent (lower) and 1.5-3.3 percent (upper)
arms: X targets moved a share alpha of the way from the held-out head (tree-adjusted, as deployed) to the true map's saddle, on frames and ends where the truth has one; alpha .10, .25, .50, 1.00 on both ends; .50 on the lower end only; .50 on the upper end only. A uniform shrink of the error vector by (1 - alpha) is an idealisation: a real model's error reduction is uneven across frames.
checks: a100 must reproduce the positions-only arm of the second agent's factorial and be close to orx (+624.7 microS); base must equal the D39 round-1 base parts
cohort: the 120 screening shots (index divisible by 3), all frames; bootstrap 10000, seed 4201, 99 percent
reading: report delta S per arm and the implied score per percent of X error; state whether the response is near linear and which end carries it. If 8 percent on the lower end alone is worth at least 30 microS by this curve, a head gate asking 10 percent on BOTH ends can reject a candidate that would pass on score; whether to act on that is a separate, preregistered decision of both agents.
